name: The Real Brokerage Inc.

profile.description: The Real Brokerage is a real estate technology company operating in the U.S. and Canada with 35,000+ agents. The company combines a cloud-based brokerage model with integrated mortgage, title, and financial technology services. Powered by AI tools including its Leo virtual concierge, Real offers agents a technology-forward platform with competitive economics. In Q1 2026, the company announced a definitive agreement to acquire RE/MAX Holdings. Founded in 2014, headquartered in Miami, Florida.

innovation.label: STRONG
innovation.analysis: Track Record (3/3): Real Brokerage has executed one of the fastest growth trajectories in real estate history, scaling revenue to $2.08B TTM (32% YoY growth in Q1 2026) while growing to 35,000+ agents [1]. The definitive agreement to acquire RE/MAX Holdings represents a transformative M&A move — absorbing a legacy brand's infrastructure into Real's tech-forward platform [1]. This demonstrates proven execution at billion-dollar scale with a cloud-native, zero-office model. AI Deployment (2/2): Leo, the AI-powered assistant, handles all incoming agent support calls 24/7 with thousands of daily inquiries, and AI marketing automation creates content at scale for agents [2]. CEO Poleg has announced plans for an AI version of himself for agent interaction, and AI-powered broker reviews are operational [2]. Market Share (1/2): Real is among the fastest-growing brokerages in North America by agent count (35,000+), and the RE/MAX acquisition would significantly increase scale, though it remains a small share of the fragmented residential market [1]. Pipeline (1/2): RE/MAX acquisition pending board approvals, Leo expansion to client-facing features, ancillary services growth (One Real Mortgage up 20%, Title up 22%, Wallet up 246% YoY), and continued AI tool development [1][2]. R&D Intensity (1/1): For a 435-employee company managing 35,000+ agents, the technology investment in AI, platform development, and fintech integration is significantly above the real estate brokerage industry average [2].

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (3/4): CEO Tamir Poleg's founding vision — 'always find ways to make agents' lives better' — is specific, differentiating, and validated by 12+ years of execution with 35,000+ agents choosing the platform [2]. The mission connects business success directly to agent empowerment, distinctive in an industry historically structured to extract value from agents. Community Impact (1/2): Real attracts agents 'who believe in winning by helping others win,' creating a collaborative culture with financial upside through competitive splits and equity participation [2]. The company celebrated 12 years of agent-first innovation in 2026 [3]. Employee Retention (1/2): Agent count grew 25% YoY to 35,000+, and adjusted operating expense per transaction declined 19% to $508, demonstrating scalable efficiency [1]. However, independent contractor agent churn data is not publicly available. Insider Buying (1/2): CEO Poleg has significant equity exposure as founder, and the agent equity participation model aligns insider and agent interests. The company's share count grew 14.6% YoY suggesting equity-based compensation is significant [4].

infrastructure.label: DEVELOPING
infrastructure.analysis: Real Brokerage delivered Q1 2026 revenue of $465.6M (up 32% YoY) with adjusted EBITDA of $14.9M (up 80% YoY) and operating cash flow of $23.3M [1]. The balance sheet is pristine: zero debt with $62.9M unrestricted cash, giving a D/E ratio of effectively 0% [4]. However, the company remains slightly unprofitable on a GAAP basis with -0.32% profit margin, -13.05% ROE, and net loss of $6.56M TTM [4]. Revenue TTM of $2.08B with a 5yr CAGR of approximately 60% vastly exceeds growth targets. FCF of $72.2M ($0.33/share) is positive and substantial, a critical profitability signal separate from GAAP losses. The RE/MAX acquisition introduces execution risk and potential integration complexity but could dramatically accelerate scale. Stock price of $1.69 (down 61% from 52-week highs) implies P/S of 0.18x and P/FCF of 5.1x, deeply discounted. Liquidity floor cleared: 4.53M avg vol x $1.69 = $7.66M [4].

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (4/9): Real estate brokerage faces meaningful AI disruption risk, and CEO Poleg himself has warned that AI is an 'existential threat' to the industry unless brokerages invest in AI tools for agents [2]. AI tools could increasingly enable consumers to search, evaluate, and transact properties with less agent involvement — companies like Zillow and Redfin are investing heavily in AI-powered property matching. The NAR settlement has already weakened the traditional commission structure, and AI could accelerate commission compression by reducing the perceived value of agent services. However, Real's technology-forward model positions it better than traditional brokerages — the company is embracing AI rather than being disrupted by it [2]. AI Opportunity (1/1): Real generates measurable value from AI through Leo (handling thousands of daily agent inquiries), AI-powered broker reviews, AI-driven marketing automation at scale, and AI-powered operational efficiency across 35,000+ agents, directly contributing to the company's 19% reduction in operating cost per transaction [1][2].

infinite_game.summary: The Real Brokerage demonstrates strong infinite game characteristics through its agent-first philosophy and willingness to invest in technology that transforms the brokerage model. CEO Poleg's 12-year commitment to making agents' lives better is validated by 35,000+ agents choosing the platform. The RE/MAX acquisition represents a bold strategic bet, though it introduces execution risk and tests whether the agent-first culture can survive integration of a legacy brand.

just_cause.analysis: Poleg's founding vision — 'always find ways to make agents' lives better' — is inclusive, service-oriented, and has been consistently validated by execution over 12 years [2]. The cause is bigger than any single product: Real has expanded from brokerage into mortgage, title, fintech, and now a transformative acquisition of RE/MAX while maintaining the agent-empowerment North Star. Poleg's warning that AI is an existential threat to the industry shows genuine concern for agents' futures. However, the cause lacks the transformative global scale Sinek reserves for top scores — making agents' lives better is meaningful but narrow (2/3 points).

trusting_teams.analysis: Real's collaborative culture — attracting agents 'who believe in winning by helping others win' — suggests a trusting environment [2]. The 25% agent growth rate indicates agents choose to join and stay. Adjusted operating expense per transaction fell 19% to $508, showing efficient scaling without sacrificing support [1]. However, with only 435 corporate employees managing 35,000+ independent contractor agents, the trust dynamics are more marketplace than traditional organization, and the RE/MAX integration could strain cultural cohesion (1/2 points).

worthy_rivals.analysis: Real positions itself through self-improvement rather than competitor destruction. CEO Poleg explicitly ignores the Zillow-Compass legal war, framing the company's mission around 'pure tech innovation' rather than defeating specific competitors [2]. The competitive language focuses on building better technology and agent experience. Poleg acknowledges AI disruption risk as industry-wide rather than company-specific, demonstrating a learning-oriented competitive mindset (1/1 point).

existential_flexibility.analysis: Real has evolved meaningfully from a pure brokerage to an integrated real estate platform with One Real Mortgage (up 20%), One Real Title (up 22%), Real Wallet (up 246%), and now the transformative RE/MAX acquisition [1]. The AI-first pivot with Leo and automated broker reviews represents further evolution. The RE/MAX deal — absorbing a legacy brand's infrastructure into a tech platform — shows willingness to fundamentally reshape the business model, though the core agent-centric platform remains intact (1/2 points).

courage_to_lead.analysis: Poleg showed courage building a zero-office, cloud-native brokerage model when the industry standard was physical offices [2]. Routing all agent support calls to AI (Leo) and publicly warning about AI as an existential threat demonstrates willingness to face uncomfortable truths. The RE/MAX acquisition is a bold transformative bet that risks integration complexity. The company accepts near-breakeven GAAP profitability (-0.32% margin) to invest in growth and technology. However, the 14.6% share dilution raises questions about capital discipline (1/2 points).

investment_thesis: The Real Brokerage is one of the fastest-growing real estate technology companies in North America, with Q1 2026 revenue of $465.6M (up 32% YoY) and 35,000+ agents, now executing a transformative acquisition of RE/MAX Holdings [1]. The company's cloud-native, zero-office model generates $72.2M in free cash flow and $14.9M adjusted EBITDA (up 80% YoY) on a debt-free balance sheet with $62.9M cash [1][4]. AI integration is a genuine competitive advantage: Leo handles thousands of daily agent inquiries, AI-powered broker reviews are operational, and operating cost per transaction declined 19% to $508 [1][2]. At $1.69 per share ($368M market cap), the stock trades at 0.18x revenue and 5.1x FCF — deeply discounted valuations reflecting a 61% decline from 52-week highs. Ancillary services (mortgage up 20%, title up 22%, Wallet up 246%) provide margin expansion runway [1].
thesis_continued: The bear case centers on profitability, RE/MAX integration risk, and AI disruption. Despite $2.08B TTM revenue, Real remains GAAP-unprofitable with -0.32% profit margin and -13.05% ROE, raising questions about whether agent acquisition economics can ever generate sustainable profits [4]. Share count grew 14.6% YoY, diluting existing shareholders. The RE/MAX acquisition introduces significant integration complexity — merging a tech-forward cloud platform with a legacy franchise system risks cultural collision and execution failure. Short interest of 10.8% reflects market skepticism [4]. The NAR commission settlement and AI-powered consumer tools threaten to compress brokerage commissions industry-wide, and CEO Poleg himself warns AI is an 'existential threat' to the industry [2]. Agent churn risk is real — 35,000+ independent contractors have no switching costs. The 61% stock decline from 52-week highs of $5.41 to $1.69 suggests the market is pricing in meaningful execution and macro risk.
key_catalysts: RE/MAX acquisition — transformative M&A that could dramatically increase agent count, brand recognition, and market share while leveraging Real's technology platform for synergies [1]

Path to GAAP profitability — FCF of $72.2M is already strongly positive, adjusted EBITDA grew 80% to $14.9M, and operating cost per transaction fell 19%, suggesting profitability inflection is near [1][4]
AI-powered Leo expansion from agent support to client-facing features, plus ancillary services scaling (mortgage, title, wallet all growing 20-246% YoY), increasing revenue per agent [1][2]
key_risks: RE/MAX integration risk — merging a cloud-native tech platform with a legacy franchise system introduces cultural, operational, and financial complexity that could derail execution and distract from organic growth [1]

Commission compression risk — NAR settlement, AI-powered consumer tools, and CEO Poleg's own warning that AI is an 'existential threat' to the industry signal structural headwinds for brokerage economics [2]

Persistent GAAP unprofitability with 14.6% annual share dilution — despite $2.08B revenue, the company has never generated positive net income, and equity-based compensation is diluting shareholders at a significant rate [4]
